recipes.name: Candied Orange Peel
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet and chewy with the bitter, perfumed edge of orange peel.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly sugar, used in small amounts in cakes and pastries; the peel brings a little fiber.

ingredients.cutPrep: peel of about 5 oranges, cut in strips or dice

ingredients.prepNote: 500 g for the syrup, 125 g to roll
ingredients.note: 500 g for the syrup, 125 g to roll

instructions: Cover the peel with cold water, bring to a boil and boil for 10 minutes, then drain. Repeat twice more with fresh water each time, pouring each water away.
Dissolve 500 g sugar in the 300 ml water, add the peel and simmer very gently until the peel is translucent, about 1 hour.
Lift out the peel, roll it in the last 125 g sugar and dry on a rack overnight. Keep in a closed jar for months. Any syrup left in the pan can be kept for sweetening drinks.

citations.source: Tara's Multicultural Table, Candied Citrus Peel

recipes.curationNote: Tara's Multicultural Table, Candied Citrus Peel for every amount and step; peel of 4 oranges with 400 g sugar and 240 ml water for the syrup and 100 g to roll; scaled by 5/4 to our 5 oranges.

recipes.name: Apricot Jam
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet and tangy, with soft pieces of apricot.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly sugar; apricots bring some carotenes and fiber. A spoonful sweetens with fruit as well as sugar.
instructions: Put two or three small plates in the freezer for testing the set.
Combine the apricots, sugar and lemon juice in a large heavy pan. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Boil for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often and skimming off the foam, until the fruit breaks down and the jam coats a spoon.
Test the set: it is ready at 220°F (104°C), or when a teaspoon on a frozen plate wrinkles after a minute when pushed. If not, boil 5 minutes more and test again.
Ladle into hot clean jars, leaving ¼ inch of space at the top, and close. Process 10 minutes in a boiling water bath to keep on the shelf, or keep in the fridge and use within a month.

nutritionHighlights.note: Most of each tablespoon is sugar.
A little, from the apricots' carotenes.

recipes.curationNote: Alphafoodie, Easy apricot jam (no pectin) for every amount and step; 4.8 lb (about 2.18 kg) whole apricots, 3.3 lb (about 1.5 kg) sugar and ⅓ cup lemon juice for 9 half-pint jars; our 1 kg of pitted apricot is about 1.08 kg whole, about half the source.

recipes.name: Raspberry Jam
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, sharp and deeply fruity, with the seeds left in.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly sugar, with some fiber from the seeds.
instructions: Put two small plates in the freezer for testing the set.
Put the raspberries and sugar in a large heavy pot and crush them gently with a potato masher, leaving some whole if you like.
Stir in the lemon juice. Bring to a full rolling boil, stirring all the time, and skim off the foam.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until the jam coats the back of a spoon.

Take the pot off the heat. Put a teaspoon of jam on a cold plate, freeze it for 1 to 2 minutes and push it with a finger: it is ready when it wrinkles, or at 220°F (104°C). If not, cook a few minutes more and test again.

Ladle into warm clean jars, leaving ¼ inch (0.5 cm) of space at the top, and seal. Keeps 3 to 4 weeks in the refrigerator or up to 6 months frozen; jars processed for 10 minutes in a boiling water bath keep 12 to 18 months in a cool dark place.
recipes.curationNote: Alphafoodie, Easy raspberry jam (no pectin) for every amount and step; made at the source size: 2.2 lb raspberries, 28 oz sugar, ¼ cup lemon juice, about six 250 ml jars.

recipes.name: Red Currant Jelly
recipes.flavorProfile: Clear, tart and sweet, used with game and in sauces as much as on bread.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly sugar, with the tartness of currants.
instructions: Rinse the currants and put them in a pot with the water. Simmer for about 30 minutes, mashing them near the end, until very soft.
Pour into a jelly bag and let it drip overnight. Do not squeeze the bag, or the jelly turns cloudy.
Measure the juice. Use 450 g of sugar for every 600 ml of juice.

Bring the juice to a full rolling boil, stir in the sugar until it dissolves, and boil for about 10 minutes, until it reaches 220°F (105°C) or a drop on a frozen plate wrinkles when pushed after 30 seconds.
Take it off the heat for a minute, skim the surface, and ladle into warm sterilized jars with ¼ inch of space at the top. Seal. Processed in a water bath, it keeps about a year.
recipes.curationNote: Lovely Greens, Redcurrant jelly for every amount and step; 1 kg redcurrants with 500 ml water; sugar is 450 g for every 600 ml of strained juice, which for this batch comes to about 600 g.

recipes.name: Vanilla Ice Cream
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich and smooth, a custard base with clear vanilla.
recipes.healthBenefit: A dessert: it brings calcium and vitamin A from the milk and cream along with a fair amount of sugar and saturated fat.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Heat the milk and cream until steaming.
Whisk the yolks, sugar and salt, pour in the hot milk while whisking, return to the pan and stir over low heat until it coats a spoon (about 180°F (82°C)). Do not let it boil.
Strain, stir in the vanilla and chill overnight.
Churn in an ice cream maker and freeze until firm.

citations.source: Taste of Home, Best Ever Vanilla Ice Cream

recipes.curationNote: Taste of Home, Best Ever Vanilla Ice Cream for every amount and step; 2 cups cream, 2 cups milk, 6 yolks, ¾ cup sugar, ⅛ tsp salt, 1 vanilla bean or 3 tsp extract; matches our size.

recipes.name: Marzipan
recipes.healthBenefit: More than half almonds, so it brings vitamin E, magnesium and mostly unsaturated fat along with the sugar.

ingredients.prepNote: boiled and cooled, or rose water

instructions: Grind the almonds and sugar together in a food processor until fine and starting to clump.
Add the vanilla, then the water a little at a time, and knead into a smooth, firm paste.
Wrap tightly and keep in the fridge for up to a month.
recipes.curationNote: Cakesperiments, Homemade Marzipan (Almond Paste) for every amount and step; 200 g almonds, scaled by 1.25 to our 250 g.

recipes.name: Pork Blood Cake (Huyết)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft and silky like firm tofu, mild and faintly mineral.
recipes.healthBenefit: Very rich in iron, most of it heme iron, which the body takes up more easily than plant iron.

ingredients.prepNote: fresh, strained; bought already treated with salt by the seller
one part water to one part blood, up to one and a half parts for a softer set
the salt the seller stirs into the blood to keep it liquid

instructions: Ask the seller how much salt went into the blood. If it is very salty, use more water.
Stir the water into the blood, one part water to one part blood, or up to one and a half parts water for a softer set. Add the MSG.
Stir gently and evenly, then cook over low heat with the pot uncovered. A lid or high heat makes it porous and dry.
Let it boil for 5 to 6 minutes, then turn off the heat and leave it in the pot for 8 to 10 minutes more, until set through.
Cool, cut into cubes and keep in the fridge up to 3 days. Warm through in the soup just before serving. One serving is 100 g.

nutritionHighlights.note: Blood is one of the richest food sources of heme iron.

citations.source: VnExpress: Cách làm đông tiết đã hãm

recipes.curationNote: VnExpress, Cách làm đông tiết đã hãm for every amount and step; a method with a ratio, not a fixed yield; 1 liter of blood and 1 liter of water set to about 2 kg, so 20 servings of 100 g.
